extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and writers of experimental/antirealist fiction; narratologists
extracted.subtask_description: A framework for analyzing and evaluating 'unnatural' or antimimetic fiction — narratives that violate realist conventions — by identifying modes, features (voices/events/frames), and alternative evaluative criteria to replace standard mimetic judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unnatural narrative definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An unnatural narrative is 'one that contains significant antimimetic events, characters, settings, or frames.' It violates the implicit contract of realism — that fiction depicts what could happen in the world as we know it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition as the threshold test: identify whether the work contains significant antimimetic elements (events/characters/settings/frames). If so, treat it as an unnatural narrative rather than applying realist standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify narrative mode (mimetic / non-mimetic / anti-mimetic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish among three modes: (1) Mimetic — realism aiming to represent the world as we experience it; (2) Non-mimetic — conventional fantasy or SF that departs from realism but maintains internal consistency; (3) Anti-mimetic / Unnatural — actively violates conventions of realism without offering a substitute logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before evaluation, determine the work's mode. Mimetic criteria apply to mode (1); non-mimetic works are judged by internal rule consistency; genuinely anti-mimetic works require alternative criteria because they subvert or refuse a substitute system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antimimetic events (feature checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Events that contravene realist expectation: acausal sequences, logical impossibilities, reversals of physical law, characters who know they are characters, narratives that pause to contradict themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list to identify concrete manifestations of unnaturalness. Presence of such events signals that mimetic plausibility is not the relevant standard; evaluate how these events function in the text instead of merely marking them as 'errors'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antimimetic frames (structural violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame-level devices that disrupt realist framing: story-within-story collapses, narrator becoming character of own narration, endings that unwrite the story, multiple incompatible endings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how structural/frame violations affect the narrative's operation and meaning (do they destabilize reading, reveal artifice, generate new interpretive possibilities?). Frames are key loci where antimimetic logic is performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unnatural narrative voices (voice/point-of-view types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voices that conventional narratology struggles to account for: second-person narration ('you'), 'we' narration (collective first person), multiperson narration (shifts among persons without clear motivation), impossible narrators (beyond death, objects), multiple contradictory narrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog voice strategies to understand how perspective produces unnaturalness; ask whether voice choices create ambiguity of address/identity, collective subjectivity, or ontological impossibility and how those effects contribute to meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity of the violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the antimimetic move generate meaning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the violation is generative — producing insights, formal effects, thematic resonance, or cognitive work — rather than gratuitous. Productive violations justify departures from realist expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained logic of unnaturalness
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work establish what kind of unnatural it is?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when refusing mimetic logic, successful unnatural works often sustain their own internal logic or patterning of violation. Assess whether the text coherently organizes its antimimetic moves so readers can recognize the specie of unnaturalness at work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader cognition and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the reader engage productively with impossibility, or does the work merely confuse?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the cognitive effects on readers: productive puzzlement, reorientation of expectations, or merely bafflement. Good unnatural fiction prompts interpretive work rather than leaving the reader stranded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic / intellectual yield
rubrics_metrics.description: What is gained that mimetic fiction cannot deliver?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the unique aesthetic or intellectual returns of the antimimetic strategies — e.g., new ways to think about identity, temporality, authorship, or representation — and weigh these gains against costs in readability or coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to convention (dependence on recognizable norms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every antimimetic move depends on the convention it violates being recognizable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how effectively the work positions the reader to notice the violated convention; the meaningfulness of a violation presumes a prior familiarity with (or clear signaling of) the norm it subverts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability of mimetic criteria to unnatural works
rubrics_metrics.description: Mimetic criteria (plausibility, consistency, character motivation) do not apply to genuinely unnatural narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reject an unnatural work solely because it fails realist standards. Instead, translate evaluation into the alternative criteria above (productivity, sustained logic, reader cognition, yield, relation to convention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple contradictory narrators as a diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of two narrators giving irreconcilable accounts of the same events — not merely unreliable narration but incompatible narratorial realities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a sign of radical antimimetic strategy: assess how contradiction functions (e.g., to pluralize truth, destabilize chronology, question causality) rather than attempting to reconcile accounts into a single 'true' version.
